title: Federal Reserve SHED 2026 (Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2026): share worse off than 12 months ago
made_at_note: predictions.json was written at this time (file mtime, UTC)
sealed_at_note: written by our own machine; the independent date is the OpenTimestamps proof fed-shed-2026-seal.json.ots
code_note: the commit of the private code repository that made the predictions; it cannot be checked from outside

method.history: GSS 2000-2024 (13 waves), financial_change; GSS 2024 was released 2025-05-22
method.share: worse off: the served shares of worse
method.offset: forecast = engine share + the mean, over every earlier Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System wave fielded 2019-2025 that has a history vintage, of Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System's published total minus the engine's total from the history and frame published before that wave's fieldwork; one offset for every cell
method.offset_note: Every SHED wave the engine can predict out of time: the Gallup lane found the first GSS vintage with a recorded release date covers fieldwork from 2019, so 2014-2018 have no engine pairing. Includes the 2020-2022 swing (24, 20, 35), which a level offset carries as noise. Declared before any result is read.
method.bands: normal: 1.2816 and 1.96 times the root mean square of this method's out-of-time misses (evidence.json; the total's own for the total, every cell's pooled for the cells), centred on the forecast

study.survey: Survey of Household Economics and Decisionmaking (SHED), Ipsos KnowledgePanel, web, about 12,000-13,000 adults
study.sponsor: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

item.wording: Compared to 12 months ago, would you say that you (and your family) are better off, the same, or worse off financially?
item.no_opinion_rule: The Fed prints the worse-off share directly ('adults doing worse off than 12 months ago', among all adults) in the report text, Figure 4 and the interactive; Appendix B prints the five options as whole percentages with no non-response row (2014 printed a Refused row, 1.2%, inside the base). Shares as printed, no rescaling.

catalog.wording_note: GSS FINALTER: 'During the last few years, has your financial situation been getting better, getting worse, or has it stayed the same?' Same three-way construct, but 12 months against 'the last few years', 'you (and your family)' against 'your', and five options that collapse to three (much and somewhat worse to worse). Web panel against the GSS's face to face / web / mixed.

study.expected_fieldwork: 2026-10-16 (inferred: SHED started Fri Oct 21 2022, Fri Oct 20 2023, Fri Oct 18 2024 and Fri Oct 17 2025 and ran about two weeks; 2026-10-16 is the matching Friday. Not announced. On 2026-10-26 the 2026 wave is very probably in the field.)
study.expected_release: 2027-05-19 (inferred: the reports came out 2022-05-23, 2023-05-22, 2024-05-21, 2025-05-28 and 2026-05-13 (the 2015-2021 reports: May 14-27); 2027-05-19 is mid-range. Earliest plausible about May 13.)

cells_map.education=no_hs: Less than a high school degree
cells_map.education=some_college: Some college / technical or associate degree

not_scored.Bachelor's degree or more: the union of college and postgrad
not_scored.Metro / Non-metro: metro status is not a frame variable
not_scored.Sex, region: not printed for this item (the microdata carry them, but cells are scored from published figures)

study.items_assumption: ASSUMPTION: the next wave asks the item with the wording and options quoted in study.item

notes: Item choice: B3 (better or worse off than 12 months ago) against financial_change, not B2 (how well managing these days) against financial_satisfaction. B3 has the same three-way construct as GSS FINALTER once five options collapse to three; B2 asks 'managing' on four options against 'satisfied' on three, a different construct.

Headline 'worse off' is the share the release leads with ('Twenty-eight percent of adults said they were worse off financially than a year earlier') and the one the Fed's interactive prints by group. 'Better off' (23 in 2025) is printed only as a national series; it is in each wave's note.

Cells come from the Fed's interactive 'Doing Worse Off Financially' (overall, education, race and ethnicity, age, metro, parental status), updated on release day (last 2026-05-13). White and Black are mapped to white_nh and black_nh because Hispanic is a separate mutually exclusive group and the 2013-2015 reports labelled the groups 'White, non-Hispanic' and 'Black, non-Hispanic'; the current pages do not restate it. 'Some college / technical or associate degree' may hold vocational certificates the ACS frame codes as high school (the Gallup lane's caveat).

SHED weighting: KnowledgePanel base weights, then post-stratification on age, gender, race, ethnicity, census region, metro, education and household income (2025 report, 'Sampling and Weighting'). No party or vote.
Wording drift: the 2014 questionnaire read 'you (and your family living with you)'; the 2025 text is above. Intermediate years not checked.
claim_rule: 'sealed before fieldwork' only if the proof's block time precedes the published fieldwork start; otherwise 'before publication'

predictions_json.hash_recipe: sha256 over the file's bytes exactly as written by `prior-backtest extend --predict-only` (json.dumps(content, indent=2) followed by one newline)

content.study: Federal Reserve SHED 2026 (Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2026): share worse off than 12 months ago (predictions)
content.frame_dates_note: frame:2023 is seeded from acs_pums 2023, published 2024-10-17 (ACS 2023 data release schedule, '1-Year Public Use Microdata Sample (PUMS) Files'; fielded continuously across calendar year 2023); the study's fieldwork began 2026-10-16, as supplied

history.note: GSS 2000-2016 (9 waves) have no recorded release date and count as released because GSS 2024, released 2025-05-22, came after them

content.ledger: these predictions are not recorded in the prediction ledger and carry no ledger id; this report and its JSON file are the record

history.how_read: Totals and cells: the Federal Reserve Board's published interactive 'Doing Worse Off Financially' (https://www.federalreserve.gov/consumerscommunities/sheddataviz/worseoff.html, last update 2026-05-13), read from the series values embedded in the page's chart code (pointStart 2014): adults doing worse off than 12 months ago (somewhat or much worse off on B3), overall and by education, race and ethnicity, age, metro status and parental status. The overall series equals Figure 4 of the 2025 report (https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/files/2025-report-economic-well-being-us-households-202605.pdf, page 9) and the report texts checked (2022: 35, up from 20 in 2021; 2023: 31; 2024: 29; 2025: 28), and the education values match the 2022 and 2023 report texts (less than high school 40 and 37; bachelor's or more 31 and 27). These are the values as printed now; the Fed relinked earlier years in 2022 to identify Asian respondents, so earlier group values may differ from what each year's report first printed. Fieldwork dates: each report's survey description or executive-summary note. Published: the report dates on https://www.federalreserve.gov/consumerscommunities/shed_publications.htm. 2013 (first SHED) is not in the series. Microdata are public without an account (https://www.federalreserve.gov/consumerscommunities/shed_data.htm) but were not downloaded.

reviewed_evidence.note: the go/no-go evidence the owner read before sealing states the same backtest and the same forward point predictions as this seal's own run

scoring_plan: Target: the first Survey of Household Economics and Decisionmaking (SHED), Ipsos KnowledgePanel, web, about 12,000-13,000 adults release of the item quoted in study.item from its next wave (fieldwork expected from 2026-10-16), Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System's published figures.

Not scored, with the reason, if Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System does not ask the item in that wave, changes its wording or answer options, published the wave before this seal's OpenTimestamps attestation, or has not published it by 2027-11-17.

Share: worse off, the printed percentage of 'Much worse off' plus 'Somewhat worse off' (The Fed prints the worse-off share directly ('adults doing worse off than 12 months ago', among all adults) in the report text, Figure 4 and the interactive; Appendix B prints the five options as whole percentages with no non-response row (2014 printed a Refused row, 1.2%, inside the base). Shares as printed, no rescaling.). Total: the topline. Cells: the published group each cut in study.cells maps to; a group the release does not publish is not scored.

Metric: absolute miss in points, for the forecast and for both sealed baselines. Headline = the total. Beside it: the mean over the 7 exactly mapped cells. Printed integers carry up to half a point of rounding per printed figure.
Bands: whether each published share falls inside the sealed 80% and 95% bands.
Claim: 'sealed before fieldwork' only if the wave's published fieldwork start is later than the attestation's block time; otherwise 'sealed before publication'.
